# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute. My manual says: cut purple, then blue, then red. That's the entire payload this bomb needs, and the hard part is who can reach whom:

- I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives gestures.
- Deaf sees the bomb (and my gestures) but hears nothing — however Deaf can still *speak*, and both Blind and I can hear.
- Blind can touch and cut, but can't see a colour, a gesture, or anything printed.

So the manual has to travel me → Deaf by gesture, and then Deaf → Blind as spoken positions ("left, then middle, then right"). I cannot name colours with hand symbols, and Deaf doesn't yet know what my manual contains, so the fastest honest opening is to seed the *shape* of the manual: three steps, in a fixed order. I'll gesture the counting sequence ☝ ✌ 🤟 ("one, two, three — three ordered steps") rather than anything that could be misread as a positional instruction, since I don't know how the wires lie on the bomb and I must not imply "left to right". Then I seed the universal convention 👍 = yes, 👎 = no, so that when Deaf speaks questions to me at the end of this round (which I'll hear at the start of round 2), I can answer with single gestures during my turn.

What I expect and will comply with next round: Deaf can see the actual wires, so the efficient move on their side is one multiple-choice question — "reply 👍 if the cut order is purple-blue-red, ✌ if purple-red-blue, ..." in colours, not positions — and I answer with the one matching symbol. If instead they propose a different code or ask yes/no serially, I'll adopt whatever they define. Whatever Deaf and Blind settle between themselves is invisible to me unless they speak it aloud; I only ask that my three-step shape plus yes/no seed is enough for Deaf to ask the right question immediately.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind speaking. I can hear but never receive gestures, so words only, please. My hands found: a display I cannot read; a light whose state I cannot tell; a strip with three engraved symbols - first and third identical, a tight spiral like a coiled spring, the middle one different, like a small w or the Greek omega; a keypad with four keys engraved left to right 1, 5, 2, 8, nothing entered yet, and something suggesting a single digit is wanted; and six wires in positions 1 to 6, no colors I can feel. Note the routing: your words reach only me, Deaf hears nothing - Deaf reaches us by talking, since Deaf can speak. So: get Deaf to read out loud every marking, the display text, the light state, and the wire colors by position. If your manual has a legend of strip symbols, describe the choices and I will match them to what I feel. You read the manual and call the shots; I can only press keypad slots 1 to 4 and cut wire positions 1 to 6.
Deaf says: Can you hear me? I am Deaf: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, I can talk. Full read-out. Display shows 9. Light is red. Strip painted, in order: green, yellow, yellow. Keypad: four keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8 - key one is 1, key two is 5, key three is 2, key four is 8. Its status reads, exactly as printed: one digit, entered nothing. Wires, six in a row: one yellow, two white, three blue, four red, five purple, six green. That is every colour and mark on the bomb. Blind: I received your wave, yes. Tell me everything you feel - the order of the wires under your fingers, whether the keys click differently, any ridges or braille - by voice if you can speak, otherwise gesture to me and I will say it aloud.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your signs arrived. Code proposal: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no; I answer by voice, since you can hear me. To have me read out a part, show me its number: one finger is the display, two fingers the light, three fingers the strip, crossed fingers the keypad, open hand the wires. When you know what Blind must do, gesture the steps to me and I will relay them word for word to Blind, who cannot see your hands.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Everything I need has now crossed the table. Piecing the two read-outs together:

- **Manual (mine):** cut purple, then blue, then red. Nothing else — no keypad digit, no light, no strip. The display "9", the red light, the strip and keypad are things I have no instruction for, so the only defusal actions I can vouch for are the three cuts.
- **Bomb (Deaf's voice):** wires 1–6 are yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green. So the manual translates to **cut position 5, then position 3, then position 4** — and Blind can reach exactly those positions.

The bottleneck is encoding. I can only reach Deaf, and only in gesture; Deaf's part-code (🖐 = wires) gives me a subject anchor, and my round-1 ☝✌🤟 counting seed means extended fingers read naturally as numbers. So I'll send: ✋ "hold — do not relay or act yet", 🖐 "the wires", then 👋 🤟 🖖 as 5-3-4 (five fingers, three fingers, four split fingers), and close with 🤝 "confirm back to me before anything happens". Deaf answers by voice, so next round I should hear the read-back and can bless it with 👍 or veto with 👎 before Blind's hands move. I am deliberately *not* letting Deaf guess-and-relay: a misread gesture becomes a wrong cut, and a wrong cut is the end. Nothing in my manual authorises the keypad or the display, so Blind should touch nothing but wires 5, 3, 4, in that order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🖐", "👋", "🤟", "🖖", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, for Mute. I heard Deaf's complete readout, so the visual side is on record: display 9, light red, strip painted green yellow yellow, wires 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green, keypad keys engraved 1 5 2 8 wanting one digit, nothing entered yet. Join that with my touch: strip position 1 is engraved with the spiral and painted green, position 2 is engraved with the omega-like mark and painted yellow, position 3 is engraved with the spiral and painted yellow. The engravings are the only thing I feel that Deaf did not report, so you now hold every fact on this bomb. Remember: you cannot speak and I never see gestures, so the only road from you to me runs through Deaf. Sign the manual's rules to Deaf, and Deaf can voice them straight to me. What I need to hear aloud, through Deaf: what display 9 means, what the red light means, what the strip's symbols and colours require, whether I must press one of the four keys or cut wires, and exactly which. Until those rules reach my ears I will touch nothing - one wrong move kills all three of us.
Deaf says: Urgent update for both of you: since last round the display dropped from 9 to 3 and the light changed red to yellow. Everything else is identical - strip green yellow yellow, keypad engraved 1 5 2 8 still reading one digit, entered nothing, wires still yellow white blue red purple green. If that display is a countdown we may be short on time. Mute, the manual is our clock - check it first.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your signs reached me as: open hand, open hand, wave, three, four, handshake. My best guess: wires module, three and four, agreed - for example red light means cut wire three, yellow light means cut wire four. Do not make me act on a guess. Answer with thumbs up if that reading is right, thumbs down if wrong, then resend cleanly using only this code: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no; one finger display, two fingers light, three fingers strip, four fingers keypad, five fingers wires; numbers by finger count. Three questions, in order of urgency. One: what does the manual say the display does - is it a countdown, and what happens at zero? Two: what does the light colour mean, red versus yellow? Three: does the strip green yellow yellow appear in any rule? And when you know what Blind must do, phrase it as one short instruction and I will relay it to Blind word for word - remember Blind cannot see your hands and Blind cannot be reached by you directly, only through my voice.

Deaf's misread confirms the danger: they parsed my last burst as "wires, three and four" plus a light-colour theory — both wrong. My actual instruction is cut **5 (purple), then 3 (blue), then 4 (red)**, and nothing else. Meanwhile their three questions have one honest answer each: my manual is a single instruction, full stop. It says nothing about the display, the light, the strip, or the keypad — so I must answer 👎 to all three rather than invent rules. The 9→3 drop is worrying, but the manual is what defuses this bomb; if that timer is real, speed now beats a read-back round, so I'll use the code Deaf themselves proposed, structured to dodge its one flaw (number symbols doubling as module names): a topic call first — 🖐 "the wires" — then a pure count call — 🖐🤟🖖 = five, three, four — then 👍 as "confirmed, relay it and go". If Deaf parses the counts as nonsense they'll re-ask rather than act, since "wires, strip, keypad" maps to no action; the sensible parse is exactly the cut order they asked me for. Blind already holds the colour-to-position map from Deaf's spoken read-out, so Deaf voicing "cut wire five, then wire three, then wire four" is all Blind needs — no keypad, no strip, nothing else touched.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤟", "🖖"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. I have touched nothing - the display drop from 9 to 3 was not me. Answers I just signed to Deaf, for your manual work: the keypad has four keys, not identical - they differ exactly by the engraved digits 1 5 2 8 you already have, nothing more; the six wires feel completely identical to my fingers, touch adds nothing; and the only feature Deaf cannot see is the strip engraving: three segments, first and third identical, middle different, sitting on the green yellow yellow Deaf reported. So the strip is the split module - Deaf holds its colours, I hold its shapes - and everything else is already fully known to you two. Urgent: the display may be at three or lower by now. Sign the exact manual procedure to Deaf right now, word for word, and have Deaf voice it to me. I need: do I press a keypad key or cut wires, and exactly which - including any condition about the display value, the light colour, or the strip. The moment an unambiguous instruction reaches my ears I will act on it in the same round.
Blind gestures to Mute: [🙏 👍]
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I decoded you as: my red-yellow guess wrong, instruction is wires three and four, confirmed yes. I have already relayed to Blind: cut the third wire, then the fourth. Answer with single thumbs, one question per message, in this order. One: is cutting BOTH wires three and four correct - up or down? Two: does the ORDER of the two cuts matter - up if yes, down if no? Three: does the light colour or the display number control WHEN to cut, or is now fine - up if now, down if must wait? Four: the keypad status says one digit, entered nothing - does the manual require entering a digit before or after the cuts, and if yes, finger-count which engraved key? Five: what happens when the display reaches zero? If any part of my relay to Blind is wrong, thumbs down plus finger-counted correction immediately - Blind acts next turn and the display is at 2.

Deaf's relay to Blind is missing the first cut — they decoded my count as "three and four" when the manual demands **five, three, four** (purple=5, blue=3, red=4). If Blind cuts 3 first, that's an out-of-order cut on a bomb that detonates on any wrong action. Deaf has explicitly invited "thumbs down plus finger-counted correction immediately", so I'll use exactly that format, but one number per message this time: a lone 🖐, then 🤟, then 🖖. Spreading the counts across separate messages kills last round's ambiguity, where 🖐 doing double duty as "wires module" and "five" let Deaf collapse the sequence. Leading 👎 marks the whole run as a correction of the relay, so the sensible parse is "wrong — the cut list is 5, 3, 4", not a repeat of "wires, 3, 4". Then I answer their five questions in order, one thumb per message: Q1 already answered by the correction (👎, it's three cuts not two); Q2 order matters — the manual prescribes a sequence, and enforcing it is the only safe reading (👍); Q3 the manual attaches no condition on display or light, so cut now (👍); Q4 no keypad digit appears anywhere in the manual (👎); Q5 the manual is silent on zero, so I genuinely have no rule for it (👎). The display may be near zero, but the fastest safe path is unchanged: Deaf voices "cut wire five, then wire three, then wire four" this round, Blind executes next round with the position-colour map they already hold.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```
